Clause-②: no — deleting inert keys from fixtures. No schema, no accept/reject move, no published surface.
Serial constraints cleared: `examples/schema-catalog/**` — no in-flight card names it. The three cards in flight on this lane are `os-sam`'s #7004 (`cli`), #6935 (`types`) and #7094 (`domain:skills`); mine are #7086 (`scripts/` + `content/docs/api/`) and #7082 (`content/docs/components/`). All disjoint from this one.

## ZONE 1 — RULING (⛔ not re-adjudicable)

> Delete the 21 `"value"` keys. ⛔ Not "declare `value` on `MenuCommandItem`" — nothing reads it, and #6523 deliberately narrowed this union rather than widening it.

⇒ Fixtures only. ⛔ Do not touch `packages/types/src/overlay.ts`, the zod mirror, or any renderer. If the repair appears to need a type change, that is a fork — stop and report.

## ZONE 2 — PM MECHANISM ASSUMPTIONS (⚠️ re-derive; the card's own numbers are from `592acafb` and `main` has moved to `2c3cd1b`)

The card's table claims 21 occurrences across four fixtures (menubar 11, context-menu 4, dropdown-menu 3, with-icons 3). **Re-count on current `main` before and after.** ⚠️ A sibling card, #7077, independently counts `buttons[].value` in the *button-group* fixtures — a different component family. ⛔ Do not let its 17 leak into your 21; they are separate populations.

## Zero-hit discipline

Any zero you report needs a control term that must hit in the same query. After the deletion, the natural control is that `label` still hits in every file you touched.

## ⚠️ One absorber to check first

Triage's handover flags that **#6810 was never checked as a possible absorber** for this card. #6810 is the class decision card, currently scoped to the `content` key only and still undecided. If you find it has since been ruled toward a family-wide sweep, say so and stop — this card would then be a row of that sweep rather than a hand fix. If it is still undecided (which I expect), proceed: this deletion is deterministic and a later sweep would simply find nothing here.

## Premise-first

Read the card and its comments on GitHub yourself; check the body for sanitizer truncation and say you checked. `premise_still_valid: false` is a legitimate delivery. Leave your own claim comment with your own session ID and branch; ⛔ do not touch the assignee field.

⚠️ One thing I am carrying forward from that ruling rather than dropping: its prescribed shape for a newly-rediscovered key is 逐例修 **+ 补钉** — the hand fix *plus* a named pin with a counter-probe, in the existing `component-fixture-declared-keys.test.ts` ledger. ## ACCEPT WITH FOLLOW-UP — PR #7103. The fix is right; the ruling's **second half** is owed, and the dev was right to escalate rather than take it.

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`. Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

### ⛔ First: my dispatch order's stop-condition pointed the wrong way, and the dev checked anyway

I wrote *"#6810 … still undecided (which I expect)"* and set the stop-condition as **"if it has since been ruled toward a family-wide sweep, stop."**

**#6810 was ruled twice, and the second ruling went the opposite direction from the one I fenced against.** I verified it myself rather than relaying — comment `5469403582`, 2026-08-30, maintainer, verbatim「同意」:

> 1. **对「已再生过的键 × 类型对」逐对钉死** … 落点沿用既有 `component-fixture-declared-keys.test.ts` 的具名钉形制(**每钉带反探针**)
> 2. ⛔ **不建**全类型读键集提取器 … 选项 A 明确不采;从未见过的键接受 C 的默认速率(**人手撞见、逐例修 + 补钉**)

⇒ Option A (the sweep I told you to stop for) was **refused in as many words**. And the prescription for a newly-rediscovered key is **fix + pin**, not fix.

⭐ A stop-condition written against the wrong branch is worse than none, because it reads as though the space was covered. The only reason it cost nothing is that the dev read the ruling instead of pattern-matching my sentence.

### What I verified independently

| claim | my reading on the PR branch |
|---|---|
| all 21 `value` keys gone from the four fixtures | ✅ **0 hits** across all four |
| control — `label` must still hit | ✅ **14** (menubar) / **4** (context-menu) |
| scope held | ✅ 5 files: the four fixtures + changeset. ⛔ No type, no zod mirror, no renderer |
| count had not moved since the card | ✅ distribution identical file-for-file; catalog-wide `value` objects 288 → 267, **delta exactly 21**, so nothing outside the four fixtures moved |

⭐ Counting by **tree position rather than filename** is what keeps #7077's button-group population out by construction rather than by care — its files are in the catalog-wide figure and untouched.

### ⭐ The render-equivalence reading, and two negative results reported rather than buried

The expectation here is **unchanged** output — the opposite of a fixture-content fix — and that is the easy thing to assert without measuring. It was measured instead: both dropdown fixtures rendered at BASE and HEAD with `defaultOpen: true` injected (⭐ because a closed menu renders only its trigger, which never carried the key — the comparison would have been **vacuous**), Radix per-instance ids normalised, and the control mutating the *read* key `label` was required to differ and did.

And the coverage is stated honestly rather than overclaimed: the DOM measurement covers the **6** items in the two dropdown fixtures; menubar (11) and context-menu (4) cannot be forced open that way, so their inertness rests on the zero-read derivation plus the corpus suites.

Two failures caught by controls before any number was banked:
1. A first harness lacked the component-registration side-effect import and fell back to a raw-JSON dump — its control caught it.
2. An earlier version read the HEAD side via `git show :path`, which reads the **index**; with the fixture edits unstaged it would have compared BASE against itself and **passed vacuously**.

⇒ That second one is the sharpest thing in this report. A vacuous pass is indistinguishable from a real one from the outside.

### ✅ Housekeeping

Empty-frontmatter changeset with the gate's verdict line quoted · vitest root-relative with the `RUN v4.1.10 /home/user/objectui-issue-7072` banner proving no re-root onto `apps/console` · eslint plain form, narrowing proven from eslint's own config (the diff has zero JS/TS files) · #7101 and #7102 filed and correctly **not** folded in.

⭐ Deriving the gate family **by hand** from objectui's own `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` — because `dispatch-gates.mjs` lives only in `objectstack` and would have answered about that tree — is the right call and the kind of thing that usually goes unnoticed.

### The follow-up, and the fence extension that unblocks it

The ruling's pin half is owed. Your two reasons for not taking it unilaterally were both good, and they get different answers:

- **(b) upheld.** ⛔ Do **not** widen the menubar sweep. You are right that a menubar-only pin covers 11 of 21 while reading as though it covered all — worse than none — and that the sweep's own header declares it deliberately menubar-scoped.
- **(a) resolved — I am extending the fence.** My order fenced you to `src/schemas/`, and you correctly refused to write a test outside it. ⇒ **The fence is now `examples/schema-catalog/`, the same package including its `test/` directory.** That is my scope decision and it is on the record.

⇒ Patch round sent: a **separately named** corpus pin over all four overlay-menu fixtures, carrying a counter-probe that goes red when `value` is reintroduced into a fixture. ⭐ Your own datum sharpens what is missing: the file already uses `value` as a negative control at the **schema** level, so the type-level fact is pinned — **the gap is purely the corpus assertion.**

⛔ PR stays draft until that lands. ⚠️ #7102 becomes live the moment #7103 merges (two test comments naming these fixtures go false), so it wants picking up promptly — but it is `packages/components`, a different package and gate family, and stays its own card.
